In 2011, NRK took on an extremely ambitious
project—a five-and-a-half-day boat cruise along
Norway’s most famous shipping route. The Hurtigruten
voyage was broadcast live, and Norwegians did more
than watch. Some crowded the ports along the route;
some were seen standing all alone on rocky outcroppings;
others actually sailed alongside the ship. In addition to
stunning landscapes, sunsets, and coastal architecture, the
footage captured thousands of people enthusiastically
waving to compatriots watching from home. The television
audience included more than three-fifths of the country’s
five million people, an all-time high for NRK.
PASSAGE III
Goode’s Idea
On July 14, 1885, Sarah E. Goode, a furniture
store owner on Chicago’s South Side, received a US
patent—one of the first granted to an African American
woman—for her folding cabinet bed. Unlike the more
modern Murphy bed, which is stored vertically against a
wall and camouflaged as a cabinet, Goode’s bed hid inside
a free-standing cabinet that also functioned as a desk.
Meant to meet the needs of city-dwelling customers,
people whom needed furniture that maximized small
apartment spaces, Goode’s bed entered the market as the
first space-saving design of its kind.
Which choice most effectively creates a connection
between the preceding paragraph and this paragraph?
A. No Change
B.
That excitement inspired one of NRK’s most
ambitious projects—
C.
NRK’s producers undertook a very ambitious
project in 2011—
D.
Then came NRK’s ambitious Hurtigruten
project—
Which choice best maintains the stylistic pattern
established in the sentence?
F. No Change
G.
some people stood alone on rocky outcroppings;
H.
some, on rocky outcroppings, stood alone;
J.
some stood alone on rocky outcroppings;
Which choice best avoids wordiness and redundancy in
context?
A. No Change
B.
unsurpassed, record-breaking success and
achievement
C.
exceptional, incomparable, and rare triumph
D.
unusual and unprecedented event
At this point, the writer is considering adding the
following sentence to the beginning of the essay:
Many people find furniture useful.
Should the writer make this addition here?
F.
Yes, because the sentence helps establish why
Goode chose to live in Chicago and open a
furniture store.
G.
Yes, because the sentence helps establish what
type of furniture people preferred at the time.
H.
No, because the sentence is an overgeneralization
that is not specifically tied to the main subject of
the first paragraph.
J.
No, because the sentence fails to situate the reader
in history.
Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically
acceptable?
A. No Change
B.
which
C.
whom
D.
who
